title: Week of Aug 24–30
subtitle: Block 3, Big-4 retest — Week 2 (first push week), compressed for a travel weekend: lower Mon · quality run Tue · upper + ride Wed · full body Thu · progression run Fri. Two quality touches, balanced 4/4 sets, guaranteed 17 running miles by Friday.
goals: The volume question, answered with the log: last week you did ~48 working sets and ~26k lb — Block 1's calibration week was 65 sets and ~37k lb, and its build weeks ran 86–87 sets and 45–48k. So yes, you were down about 30%, and your journals called it correctly (2-set accessories, thin core). This week is rebuilt to ~73 planned sets: 4-set mains and 4-set partner lifts, 3-set accessories everywhere, a superset every lift day, and 6+ core sets every lift day. The only volume you're 'missing' vs Block 1 is the fourth barbell day — and that slot is deliberately your 25–30 mile ride.

Push week targets, straight off calibration, now balanced 4/4 per your call — every main lift ramps over 4 sets to one top set, and the extra set went to the partner lift instead of a back-off: Squat 195×5 with RDL 4×8 behind it, Bench 180×5 with strict OHP 4×5 (110 top), Deadlift 265×4. Same weekly total (~73 sets), flatter spread. Top sets at ~2 RIR, unspotted bench rules, full back protocol on every hinge.

Intensity distribution, recalibrated per your point: you're right that the hard-aerobic share has been too small, with one correction to the ledger — lifting doesn't belong in EITHER bucket. HR drifting through Z2 between sets isn't continuous aerobic work, so it doesn't count as easy volume any more than it counts as intensity; the 80/20 math should run over aerobic minutes only (runs + rides). By that ledger last week you did ~4.2 aerobic hours and about 18 hard minutes — roughly 7% hard, not 20%. So the diagnosis isn't 'too much Z2', it's that BOTH ends shrank. While running volume sits this low the rule is ~70/30 with TWO quality touches, converging back to 80/20 when Block 4 rebuilds volume. This week's hard ledger: ~20 min threshold Tue, ~30 min bike tempo Wed, ~18 min steady Fri — about 65–70 hard minutes on ~5 aerobic hours, ~23%. Strides Saturday if the travel run happens.

The compressed frame for the travel weekend: everything essential lands Mon–Fri. Wednesday is a double — upper in the morning while fresh, the 25–30 mi ride later, whenever the day allows (they don't interfere; arms don't care about bike miles and the ride doesn't care about bench). Thursday's deadlift comes the morning after the ride — warm up thoroughly and let the ramp vote; 245 is a fine cap if the legs feel Wednesday. The pull-up benchmark rides with Thursday's full body, same conditions as last week (day after an upper session), so the number stays comparable.

Core, rotated per the floor: Mon = hollow hold / bird dog / suitcase carry, Wed = ab wheel / Pallof / woodchopper, Thu (deadlift day, spine-friendly) = side plank / dead bug / hanging leg raise. Six sets minimum each lift day; Friday's mini-pump adds 4 more.
Food: maintenance, deficit 0, band 189–191 with the waist as arbiter. You're fueling PR attempts and a 2-hour ride this week — under-eating is the one way to lose both.

Running math for the travel week: Mon 1.5 + Tue 5.5 + Thu 2.5 + Fri 7.5 = 17.0 guaranteed before you leave, with Saturday's flex 3 as bonus. Progress tab note: the daily lifting volume chart is gone — in its place is an 8-week weekly volume graph, so the drop we diagnosed this week stays visible on one screen.
review: Calibration week delivered everything it needed to despite starting on an engagement weekend: Squat 185×5 easy, Bench 175×5, strict OHP 105×5 past its placeholder, Deadlift 255×4, and honest journals that reshaped this plan — the 6-set core floor and the third accessory set are your notes, now standing rules. Two honest readings to hold lightly: the pull-up benchmark at 14 (Block 2 exit was 18 — but that one came fresh on a calisthenics day; this one came the morning after a full upper session, so the trend is muddier than the number) and Thursday's intervals feeling terrible (day-after-squat legs, first outdoor speed in a month, and easy runs that have been creeping hot). Saturday's 26-mile ride with Morgan was the best kind of unplanned — legs sore, aerobic system fed. Week 2's job: move every bar 5–10 lb, put the set volume back, and make easy mean easy.

days.name: Quality Run — Controlled Threshold
warmup: 2×20s relaxed strides before the first rep

run.title: Cruise Intervals — 5.5 mi total
run.detail: 1.5 mi easy warm-up → 3 × 6 min at threshold effort (comfortably hard — short sentences, not gasps) with 2 min easy jog between → easy cool-down to round out 5.5. Last week's session kicked your butt because of day-after-squat legs and a month off speed — same legs situation today, so the assignment is CONTROL: start the first rep slower than feels right and finish each rep feeling like you could do one more. Feeling strong after rep 3? Take a 4th — the week's intensity budget has room now. If rep 1 blows past comfortably hard, cut reps to 5 min instead. The paper will look mediocre for a few more weeks; that's detraining unwinding, not your ceiling.

run.title: Ride — 25–30 mi with 2×15 min tempo
run.detail: Later in the day, separate session — lift first while fresh, ride whenever works; the ride doesn't care. Settle into a steady Z2 spin for the first ~40 min, then 2 × 15 min at tempo (brisk but sustainable — short sentences, legs working, not burning) with ~10 min easy spinning between, then steady Z2 home. Everything outside the tempo blocks stays conversational. Eat a real breakfast, fuel during anything past 90 minutes, drink more than feels necessary. One eye on tomorrow: deadlifts moved to Thursday, so if the legs feel the tempo blocks, let the ride home be genuinely easy.

run.title: Progression Run — 5.5 easy + 2 steady
detail: The week's longest run, stretched to 7.5 so the running floor doesn't depend on the travel weekend: 5.5 miles genuinely easy (≤150 — your recent 'easy' has averaged ~152, which is no-man's-land; if honest Z2 means 10:30 miles right now, run 10:30 miles), then lift the last 2 miles to STEADY — Z3, comfortably brisk, ~155–165, the effort you could hold for an hour. Not threshold. The discipline is both directions — easy miles actually easy, steady miles actually steady. This closes the guaranteed 17 for the week; anything you run while traveling is bonus.

run.title: Flex Easy Run — 3 mi, travel-permitting
run.detail: If the travel day has a slot, an easy 3 anywhere — new streets are the best part of running on the road. Finish with 6 × 20s relaxed strides if there's flat ground: fast but smooth, ~85% effort, full walk-back recovery. If the day swallows it, skip guilt-free — the guaranteed 17 is already banked through Friday.

days.name: Travel — Rest
days.desc: Travel day, rest day. Walking through airports and around wherever you are counts as the recovery it is. Waist measurement if you have a tape and a quiet fasted morning; if not, take it Monday. Week 3 is the last build week of the retest — squat 200+, bench 185+, deadlift 275 are on the table Monday if this week's sets moved well.
stretches: Whatever the body asks for after travel — hips and hamstrings first
